analysis:
Examined the head text of StandaloneServer.swift lines 1220-2274 (reslice/build, eviction, acquire, ensureModelLoaded) and the LaunchAgent.swift patch. The only changed lines in the supplied file_changes are StandaloneServer.swift 562-568 and LaunchAgent.swift 282-294. The 562-568 hunk is not in the supplied text units, so the KV sweep task change is only visible as a patch excerpt.

StandaloneServer.swift: the KV sweep Task now captures [weak self] and calls retryShapeWarmups() before proactiveReclaimSweep(). The weak capture avoids a retain cycle, so I found no lifetime or security regression. The implementation of retryShapeWarmups (a GPU warmup on synthetic shapes) is not supplied, so I could not confirm it handles no user prompt content, runs only outside request serving, or cannot starve the load gate (T-029, T-010 availability). The 1220-2274 region is unchanged context. It keeps the unwind ordering, the GLM unproven-retention paths, the reservation guard against eviction races, and the pending-load budget handling.

LaunchAgent.swift: ModelCalibrationPolicy.shapeWarmupEnvironmentKey (DARKBLOOM_TTFT_SHAPE_WARMUP) is added to inferencePassthroughEnvKeys. This lets an operator env var reach the launchd job, so it is a local operator-controlled perf toggle, not a coordinator or consumer input. It is not an attestation, key or prefix-cache control. I did not see it affecting PREFIX_CACHE, T-041 TTL, salt or HMAC behavior. The definition of ModelCalibrationPolicy is not supplied, so I assume it is only an on/off flag and a fixed key string.

Open integration questions: (1) Does retryShapeWarmups run under isLoadingAny or the kvBudget activity gate, and does it avoid concurrency with load or eviction? (2) Does the warmup use only synthetic tokens, so it cannot seed the prefix cache or leak cross-tenant timing (T-041/SEC-035)? No concrete finding is supported by the supplied evidence.
